purpose: Source-verified, non-secret facts for the 1.3 checkout-path protection reader (FEATURE-PLAN.md item 5 and the protection half of item 1, contract C7). Every fact below was read from the WooCommerce release packages named in sources; citations are version:path:line with paths relative to the WooCommerce plugin root (wp- prefixed versions are WordPress core). These are source facts, not site configuration and not proof that any protection is enforced. All values in synthetic_cases are invented test shapes, never store data.

woocommerce_current.package: WordPress.org woocommerce 11.3.1 package (src/, includes/ and woocommerce.php)

wordpress.note: REST routing, batch dispatch, block delimiter and shortcode grammar. Same behaviour in 7.2-RC3 at the lines given under each fact.

verified_range.release_grammar: plain X.Y.Z only; a pre-release or build suffix is outside the range
verified_range.rule: Facts identical at both ends are used for every plain release from min to max inclusive. A fact that differs between the two ends is used only at the exact version where it was read; between them it is reported as not verified. Any version outside the range, unreadable or missing returns wc_version_unverified and no source default is assumed.

rate_limit_checkout.ui_path: WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features > Rate limit Checkout
rate_limit_checkout.option_name_rule: woocommerce_feature_{feature_id}_enabled when the definition has no option_key

saved_values.other: WooCommerce treats every value other than the string 'yes' as off; the toolkit reports any other saved value as unrecognised (state unknown, configured null), never off

rate_limit_checkout.absent_means: off by the source default, used only inside the verified range
rate_limit_checkout.methods: POST only; an X-HTTP-Method-Override header must be empty or POST
rate_limit_checkout.unanchored_note: The pattern has no end anchor, so it also matches /checkout/{id}.
rate_limit_checkout.bypass: users with the edit_posts capability are never rate limited by the Store API
rate_limit_checkout.identity: signed-in user ID, else md5 of the visitor IP address; proxy support is off by default
not_covered: checkout sub-requests sent inside the Store API batch route (outer route /wc/store/v1/batch does not match the pattern, and WordPress runs authentication once per outer request)

10.9.0.fact: feature definition, name Rate limit Checkout
enabled only when the saved value is exactly 'yes'; default 'no'
Authentication hooks only for Store API requests

11.3.1.fact: feature definition, name Rate limit Checkout
enabled only when the saved value is exactly 'yes'; default 'no'
Authentication hooks only for Store API requests

wordpress.fact: authentication runs once per outer request in serve_request

differences.fact: letter case of the request address
differences.10.9.0: case-sensitive (strpos and a pattern without the i flag) while WordPress routes in any case, so a differently cased address reaches the route outside the pattern
differences.runtime: scope_known true only at exactly 10.9.0 or 11.3.1; any version between them reports rate_limit_scope_unverified

checkout_order.authorisation: signed-in owner of a customer order; otherwise order key and billing email must match (not a bot check)

batch.methods: POST; sub-request methods POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE (filterable); sub-request paths must start with /wc/store

store_api_routes.exposure_rule: Inside the verified range these routes are available_in_core. That is a source fact, not a claim that a remote client can reach them; the toolkit never builds the REST server or dispatches a request to check.

checkout_page.page_id_filter: woocommerce_get_{page}_page_id (woocommerce_get_checkout_page_id), applied by wc_get_page_id; the toolkit reads the option and records only whether the filter has callbacks

block_marker.name: woocommerce/checkout
block_marker.rule: an opening block delimiter whose full name is exactly woocommerce/checkout (inner blocks such as woocommerce/checkout-fields-block do not count)

classic_markers.shortcode_tag_filter: woocommerce_checkout_shortcode_tag (the tag is filterable, so a renamed tag makes the classic marker unreliable)
classic_markers.shortcode_rule: [woocommerce_checkout] with or without attributes, not escaped as [[...]], not inside an HTML comment, tag not followed by a word character or hyphen
classic_markers.classic_shortcode_block: woocommerce/classic-shortcode with attribute shortcode equal to checkout; a missing attribute means cart

classic_handler.fact: the classic checkout form submits to the wc-ajax checkout event, not the Store API

types.unknown: no marker, page not set, invalid setting, missing, not published, larger than max_bytes_read, unreadable, shortcode tag renamed with no block-only marker, or WooCommerce version outside the verified range

checkout_page.template_note: WooCommerce's own block-theme checkout template renders the page content (10.9.0:templates/templates/page-checkout.html:6), but a customised theme template or page builder can change what shows; the toolkit reads the page only and says so.

order_pay.endpoint_option: woocommerce_checkout_pay_endpoint (default order-pay); not read by the toolkit

checks.11.3.1: nonce woocommerce-pay, order key, needs_payment, not a checkout draft, pay_for_order capability or email verification

order_pay.difference_note: The extra 11.3.1 checks are authorisation checks, not bot checks; the toolkit's facts for this path name only the nonce and order key, which both versions share.

add_payment_method.endpoint_option: woocommerce_myaccount_add_payment_method_endpoint (default add-payment-method); not read by the toolkit
add_payment_method.handler: WC_Form_Handler::add_payment_method_action on wp at priority 20; runs on any front-end request carrying the form fields and a valid nonce
add_payment_method.delay_key: add_payment_method_{current user ID}, so the wait is per account
add_payment_method.effective_value: not asserted; the filter can change it and the toolkit never applies it

order_attribution.note: Attribution support is reported separately from checkout-path protection: it improves evidence and does not block anything. Order-side attribution meta facts are pinned by card-testing-contracts.json.

never: render blocks, run shortcodes or apply the_content
apply any watched filter (presence only, through has_filter)
call RateLimits, WC_Rate_Limiter, Authentication, a form handler or a gateway
build the REST server or dispatch a request
read post_password or any captcha or gateway secret
enumerate option names or read options outside the four allowlisted ones
output page text, page IDs, URLs or query tokens

reason_codes.protection_enforcement_unverified: This check reads settings and the checkout page only. It cannot confirm that any protection works, and it cannot see protection added by other plugins, the server, a CDN or the payment provider.
reason_codes.wc_version_unverified: This WooCommerce version has not been checked by this tool, so its checkout routes and settings are not described.
reason_codes.checkout_page_not_set: No checkout page is set in WooCommerce.
reason_codes.checkout_page_invalid_setting: The saved checkout page setting is not a valid page.
reason_codes.checkout_page_missing: The checkout page set in WooCommerce no longer exists.
reason_codes.checkout_page_unpublished: The checkout page set in WooCommerce is not published.
reason_codes.checkout_page_oversize: The checkout page is too large for this check to read.
reason_codes.checkout_page_unreadable: The checkout page could not be read.
reason_codes.checkout_page_no_marker: The checkout page has no standard checkout block or shortcode, so a page builder, pattern or theme template may supply the checkout.
reason_codes.checkout_page_mixed: The checkout page contains both the checkout block and the classic checkout shortcode, so which one shoppers use is not known.
reason_codes.checkout_shortcode_renamed: A plugin or theme renames WooCommerce's checkout shortcode, so a classic checkout could not be recognised.
reason_codes.no_readable_protection: No setting this check can read covers this path.
reason_codes.rate_limit_checkout_off: WooCommerce's Rate limit Checkout setting is off. This does not mean nothing else protects this path.
reason_codes.rate_limit_setting_unrecognised: Rate limit Checkout has an unexpected saved value, so whether it is on is not known.
reason_codes.rate_limit_filter_present: A plugin or theme changes Store API rate limits, so the limits in use are not known.
reason_codes.rate_limit_scope_unverified: Which request addresses Rate limit Checkout matches was not checked for this WooCommerce version.
reason_codes.attribution_disabled: WooCommerce order attribution is off, so where orders came from is not recorded.
reason_codes.attribution_setting_unrecognised: The order attribution setting has an unexpected saved value, so whether it is on is not known.
reason_codes.attribution_prefix_override: A plugin or theme changes how order attribution is stored, so it could not be read.
reason_codes.attribution_fields_override: A plugin or theme changes which order attribution details are recorded, so they could not be read.
